A.explain: Consumers pay the tax to the seller — retailers and producers — who then pass it on to the government. It never goes to the government directly.
It passes through a business before reaching the government, which makes it an indirect tax rather than a direct one.

A.wrongChunk: a lower proportion of their income in consumption tax
A.correctChunk: a higher proportion of their income in consumption tax
A.explain: The same fixed tax rate takes a bigger bite out of a smaller income, so the burden lands harder on lower incomes.

A.wrongChunk: with high incomes pay a higher proportion of their income
A.correctChunk: with low incomes pay a higher proportion of their income
A.explain: Regressive is the opposite of progressive — the relatively heavier burden falls on low incomes, not high ones.

B.wrongChunk: pay a lower proportion of their income in income tax
B.correctChunk: pay a higher proportion of their income in income tax
B.explain: Income tax rates rise as income rises, so higher earners pay a larger share of their income, not a smaller one.

B.wrongChunk: with low incomes pay a higher proportion of their income
B.correctChunk: with high incomes pay a higher proportion of their income
B.explain: Progressive tax rates rise with income, so it's higher incomes that pay the larger proportion.

B.prefix: Governments combine different kinds of taxes
B.explain: Mixing direct, indirect, progressive, and regressive taxes is meant to balance who bears the burden — fairness, not lowering the total collected.

B.wrongChunk: should pay different amounts of tax
B.correctChunk: should pay the same amount of tax
B.explain: This is the principle of horizontal equity — people in the same financial position should be taxed equally.
